MIT went through more than 300 AI projects this year. 95% of the pilots they studied returned nothing anyone could measure. The AI itself worked fine. The setup around it failed, in the same three ways: It doesn't remember the business, so someone re-explains everything every day. It works in the demo and breaks with real customers. It sits in a tab nobody opens. If you've tried ChatGPT or Claude and the business still runs the way it did last year, that's why. Tomorrow night you do what the other 5% did, for one job in your business: Tell AI about your business once, so it stops starting from zero. Hand it one real job your team does every week: follow-up, the weekly report, chasing documents. Test it before you trust it, against an answer key. 90 minutes, live and hands-on, in your own Claude account, with me and my chief engineer Keshav helping.
